CLOSURE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Everything claimed holds.

Determinism - the stated proof target. n=150, p=64, two partitions, searchlight radius 2.1:
  workspace   16 MiB   bitwise identical  signature match
  workspace   64 MiB   bitwise identical  signature match
  workspace  512 MiB   bitwise identical  signature match
  workspace 4096 MiB   bitwise identical  signature match
A 256x budget range with bitwise-identical values AND identical signatures. The budget genuinely
alters cache capacity only.

Correctness against an independent base-R oracle - qr.resid(qr(X), Y) then crossprod, importing
no package code:
  run1  310 pairs  max|package - oracle| = 8.53e-14
  run2  310 pairs  max|package - oracle| = 1.14e-13
On cross-products of magnitude 100-140 that is ~1e-15 relative, i.e. floating-point exact.
residual_df = 145 = n - rank(X) on both partitions.

Pair set is exactly the union co-occurrence pattern: 310 requested, 310 upper-triangular nonzeros
in the Epic 1 support index, and every requested pair lies in the pattern.

The boundary hazard I flagged is handled: .accumulate_residual_pair_partition reads through
.residual_padded_block exclusively, with an LRU tile cache whose capacity comes from the budget.
Shape is fixed, count varies - which is the rule.

Budget refusal works and is informative: a 1 KB budget is rejected with "Canonical residual pair
accumulation requires at least 88984 bytes, exceeding the 1024-byte workspace budget", and a zero
budget is rejected. Refusal happens before source reads as claimed.

No further concerns on this bead.
